sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Back in 2018, Kurt Colstead and I went on a tour, performing a 99PI story live in cities along the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 早在2018年，库尔特·科尔斯特德和我进行了一次巡演，在东海岸的各个城市现场表演了一个《99%隐形》的故事。

sentences.en: And Swan Real and her band provided musical accompaniment.
sentences.zh: 斯旺·里尔和她的乐队提供了音乐伴奏。

sentences.en: It was so much fun.
sentences.zh: 那真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: On stage, we told the audience about a key development that helped shape a generation of modern artists and designers.
sentences.zh: 在舞台上，我们向观众讲述了一个关键的发展历程，它帮助塑造了一代现代艺术家和设计师。

sentences.en: The stage version was relatively short, but we later expanded the piece into a full episode.
sentences.zh: 舞台版本相对较短，但我们后来将其扩展成了一整集节目。

sentences.en: We have that story for you today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们为您带来那个故事。

sentences.en: With an additional, brand new, related story about how Frank Lloyd Wright's son, John, went on to create one of the most iconic building toy sets in American history.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个全新的相关故事，讲述弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的儿子约翰，是如何创造出美国历史上最具标志性的建筑玩具套装之一的。

sentences.en: That's a story that Kurt has been dying to tell for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 那是库尔特一直渴望讲述的故事，已经很久了。

sentences.en: So stay tuned for that.
sentences.zh: 所以请继续收听。

sentences.en: But first, here's Frobel's Gifts.
sentences.zh: 但首先，这是“福禄贝尔的礼物”。

sentences.en: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Friedrich Frobel.
sentences.zh: 很久很久以前，有一个叫弗里德里希·福禄贝尔的男孩。

sentences.en: His early life reads like one of those dark, old German fairy tales.
sentences.zh: 他早年的生活读起来就像那些黑暗的德国古老童话。

sentences.en: His mother died in 1783, right after he was born.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲在他出生后不久的1783年就去世了。

sentences.en: And so Friedrich Frobel had a lonely childhood.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗里德里希·福禄贝尔度过了一个孤独的童年。

sentences.en: He spent his days in the woods, looking at trees and rocks and flowers, wandering the dense forests of Thuringia in what was then Prussia.
sentences.zh: 他整天待在树林里，观察树木、岩石和花朵，漫步在当时属于普鲁士的图林根茂密森林中。

sentences.en: It's a lush region, sometimes referred to today as das Grüne Herz Deutschlands, the green heart of Germany.
sentences.zh: 那是一个郁郁葱葱的地区，有时被称为“德国的绿色心脏”。

sentences.en: That's Kurt Kolstad.
sentences.zh: 那是库尔特·科尔斯特德。

sentences.en: He produced this story.
sentences.zh: 他制作了这个故事。

sentences.en: I actually lived near Thuringia when I was a kid, and the forests there are einfach zauberhaft, simply magical.
sentences.zh: 我小时候其实住在图林根附近，那里的森林简直是魔法般的迷人。

sentences.en: And I can really see how Frobel became enthralled.
sentences.zh: 我真的能理解福禄贝尔是如何被它深深吸引的。

sentences.en: He looked at rocks, he studied the trees, he worked with a forester for a while, he was an apprentice forester.
sentences.zh: 他观察岩石，研究树木，还曾与一位林务员一起工作，做过林务员学徒。

sentences.en: That's Norman Brosterman.
sentences.zh: 那是诺曼·布罗斯特曼。

sentences.en: He's an author who studied Friedrich Frobel for years.
sentences.zh: 他是一位研究弗里德里希·福禄贝尔多年的作家。

sentences.en: Brosterman says that Frobel worked for a time as a land surveyor and even served in the military.
sentences.zh: 布罗斯特曼说，福禄贝尔曾做过一段时间的土地测量员，甚至还服过兵役。

sentences.en: He was skilled at drafting and geometry, and at one point became convinced he should be an architect.
sentences.zh: 他擅长绘图和几何，一度确信自己应该成为一名建筑师。

sentences.en: He did everything you need to become an architect.
sentences.zh: 他做了所有成为建筑师所需要做的事情。

sentences.en: He took all the right classes.
sentences.zh: 他上了所有该上的课。

sentences.en: But he didn't become an architect.
sentences.zh: 但他最终没有成为建筑师。

sentences.en: A friend convinced him to become an educator instead.
sentences.zh: 一位朋友说服他转而成为了一名教育家。

sentences.en: And in changing course, Frobel arguably ended up having more influence in the world of architecture and design than any single architect.
sentences.zh: 而正是这次转行，使得福禄贝尔在建筑和设计界产生的影响力，可以说超过了任何一位单一的建筑师。

sentences.en: And that's because Friedrich Frobel created kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 那是因为弗里德里希·福禄贝尔创造了幼儿园。

sentences.en: I believe kindergarten had a tremendous influence on the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 我相信幼儿园对20世纪产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: It impacted all parts of society, of course, including art and architecture.
sentences.zh: 它当然影响了社会的各个方面，包括艺术和建筑。

sentences.en: If you've ever looked at a piece of abstract art or modernist architecture and thought, my kindergartener could have made that.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经看过一件抽象艺术品或现代主义建筑，并心想：我上幼儿园的孩子也能做出这种东西。

sentences.en: Well, that may be more true than you realize.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那可能比你意识到的更真实。

sentences.en: The kindergarten was the product of Frobel's decades of experience in a wide range of fields.
sentences.zh: 幼儿园是福禄贝尔在多个领域积累了几十年经验的产物。

sentences.en: But the foundations of it were built on the principles of Johann Pestalozzi.
sentences.zh: 但其基础建立在约翰·裴斯泰洛齐的原则之上。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi is considered the father of modern education, which basically means they will learn better if you treat them well rather than hit them with sticks, you know.
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐被认为是现代教育之父，这基本上意味着：如果你善待孩子，而不是用棍棒打他们，他们会学得更好，你懂的。

sentences.en: In addition to the whole not hitting kids with sticks thing, Pestalozzi emphasized physical activity and active learning over rote memorization and repetition.
sentences.zh: 除了“不打孩子”这一点，裴斯泰洛齐还强调体育活动和主动学习，而不是死记硬背和机械重复。

sentences.en: And in particular, he felt that kids should draw.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他认为孩子们应该画画。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi was an early childhood educator who had incorporated pedagogical drawings in the curriculum.
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐是一位幼儿教育家，他将教学绘画纳入了课程。

sentences.en: That's author and Cooper Union professor Tamar Zinger.
sentences.zh: 那是作家兼库伯联盟学院教授塔玛·辛格。

sentences.en: And basically, he is one of the first who thought that drawing should be part of any school curriculum and should be taught to the very, very young.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他是最早认为绘画应该成为任何学校课程的一部分，并应该教给非常年幼的孩子的人之一。

sentences.en: Frobel worked for a time at a school based on these principles, and he built on what he learned from Pestalozzi,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔曾在基于这些原则的学校工作过一段时间，并在此基础上发展了他从裴斯泰洛齐那里学到的东西，

sentences.en: incorporating his own ideas along the way about how children should be taught.
sentences.zh: 同时融入了他自己关于应该如何教育孩子的想法。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi was especially busy with breaking down the two-dimensional world.
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐特别致力于拆解二维世界。

sentences.en: But what Frobel did is break down the three-dimensional world.
sentences.zh: 但福禄贝尔所做的是拆解三维世界。

sentences.en: Frobel realized he wanted kids to go beyond just drawing lines on pages.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔意识到他希望孩子们不仅仅是在纸上画线条。

sentences.en: He wanted them to learn through the physical manipulation of objects.
sentences.zh: 他希望他们通过对物体的物理操作来学习。

sentences.en: Frobel wanted children to play with toys, objects designed and crafted specifically for educational play.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔希望孩子们玩玩具，即专门为教育性游戏设计和制作的物体。

sentences.en: Now, this doesn't sound that unusual today, but it really was back in the early 1800s.
sentences.zh: 这在今天听起来并不稀奇，但在19世纪初确实非常特别。

sentences.en: Children used to go to work with their parents.
sentences.zh: 孩子们过去常常和父母一起去工作。

sentences.en: They used to sit by their parents' side and they would play with the detritus of the parents' work.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在父母身边，玩着父母工作留下的废料。

sentences.en: I mean, for example, the candle maker would make wax figurines with the leftover wax.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，例如，蜡烛制造商会用剩下的蜡制作蜡像。

sentences.en: The wooden blocks were only made from the leftover wood from the carpenter.
sentences.zh: 木块只是用木匠剩下的木头做的。

sentences.en: So it was always from the leftover material.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是来自剩余的材料。

sentences.en: Frobel wanted to build real educational intent into objects of play.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔想把真正的教育意图融入到游戏物体中。

sentences.en: But it took him decades to come to this key realization and a lot of time observing children and nature.
sentences.zh: 但他花了数十年时间才得出这个关键的认识，并花费了大量时间观察儿童和自然。

sentences.en: He was put in charge of an orphanage for a while, overseeing young children.
sentences.zh: 他曾负责管理一家孤儿院一段时间，照看年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: But he also studied the natural sciences, in particular, the emerging discipline of crystallography.
sentences.zh: 但他还研究自然科学，特别是当时新兴的学科——晶体学。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out that the man who invented kindergarten was a crystal scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，发明幼儿园的那个人是一位晶体科学家。

sentences.en: He worked with the foremost crystallographer of the time in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他在柏林与当时最顶尖的晶体学家一起工作。

sentences.en: Where most people saw nature in big, flowing, organic shapes like hills and plants and animals,
sentences.zh: 当大多数人看到的是山丘、植物和动物等宏大、流动、有机的自然形态时，

sentences.en: Frobel zoomed in to study the straight lines and the geometric forms of crystals.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔却聚焦于研究晶体的直线和几何形状。

sentences.en: To try to understand how the physical world around him is actually made.
sentences.zh: 试图理解他周围的物理世界究竟是如何构成的。

sentences.en: And Frobel came to see crystal structures as the building blocks of reality.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔开始将晶体结构视为现实的基石。

sentences.en: And this alchemy of crystals and the teaching of Pestalozzi and a childhood alone in the woods
sentences.zh: 而这种晶体炼金术、裴斯泰洛齐的教学法，以及独自在树林中度过的童年，

sentences.en: all crystallized into a solid vision.
sentences.zh: 全部结晶成了一个坚实的愿景。

sentences.en: In 1837, when he was 55 years old,
Frobel founded the very first kindergarten in Bad Blankenberg, Germany.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔在德国巴特布兰肯堡创办了第一所幼儿园。

sentences.en: And his intention was to create an educational system for children who could not yet read or write.
sentences.zh: 他的初衷是为那些还不会读写的孩子建立一套教育体系。

sentences.en: So he thought to use geometric forms as a way to teach complex and simple lessons all through play.
sentences.zh: 所以他想到利用几何形状作为一种方式，通过游戏来教授复杂和简单的课程。

sentences.en: If you can harness play, you can teach kids a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 如果你能驾驭游戏，你就能教给孩子很多东西。

sentences.en: The word kindergarten cleverly encompassed two different ideas.
sentences.zh: “幼儿园”（Kindergarten）这个词巧妙地包含了两个不同的概念。

sentences.en: Kids would play in and learn from nature.
sentences.zh: 孩子们会在自然中玩耍并向自然学习。

sentences.en: But they would also themselves be nurtured and nourished, like plants in a garden.
sentences.zh: 但他们自己也会像花园里的植物一样，得到培育和滋养。

sentences.en: And the key to it all was a set of deceptively simple-looking toys.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的关键是一套看起来简单得令人误解的玩具。

sentences.en: These were Frobel's gifts.
sentences.zh: 这就是“福禄贝尔的礼物”。

sentences.en: They're called gifts because they were to draw out the gifts of the children.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为“礼物”，因为它们旨在激发孩子们的潜能。

sentences.en: In German, of course, the phrase Frobel's gifts is rolled together into a single word.
sentences.zh: 当然，在德语中，“福禄贝尔的礼物”这个短语被合并成了一个词。

sentences.en: Frobelgaben.
sentences.zh: Frobelgaben。

sentences.en: Frobel's gifts were meant to be given in a particular order.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔的礼物需要按特定的顺序给予。

sentences.en: The toys growing more complex over time, teaching different lessons about shape, structure, and perception along the way.
sentences.zh: 玩具随着时间的推移变得越来越复杂，在此过程中教授关于形状、结构和感知的不同课程。

sentences.en: The first of Frobel's gifts was a soft, knitted ball.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔的第一份礼物是一个柔软的针织球。

sentences.en: A wool ball.
sentences.zh: 一个毛线球。

sentences.en: And it's basically the first gift a child could get at the age of six weeks.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是孩子在六周大时可以得到的第一份礼物。

sentences.en: Then the child would graduate to another ball, roughly the same size as the firSt.
sentences.zh: 然后孩子会进阶到另一个球，大小与第一个大致相同。

sentences.en: But this one is not soft, it's hard.
sentences.zh: 但这个不是软的，而是硬的。

sentences.en: A wooden, maple wooden ball.
sentences.zh: 一个枫木木球。

sentences.en: And it has a surface, it is smooth, it can roll.
sentences.zh: 它有表面，很光滑，可以滚动。

sentences.en: And then they are given the cube.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会得到一个立方体。

sentences.en: And the cube is an opposite.
sentences.zh: 立方体是球体的对立面。

sentences.en: It has sides, it has edges, it is sharp edges, it has points.
sentences.zh: 它有面，有棱，有尖锐的边缘，有顶点。

sentences.en: The cube cannot roll.
sentences.zh: 立方体不能滚动。

sentences.en: Kids are asked to enumerate the differences between the two.
sentences.zh: 孩子们被要求列举两者之间的差异。

sentences.en: And then they get a cylinder, which combines elements of both the ball and the cube.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会得到一个圆柱体，它结合了球体和立方体的元素。

sentences.en: And it blows their little minds.
sentences.zh: 这让孩子们大开眼界。

sentences.en: Each new gift would get more and more interactive and more complex.
sentences.zh: 每一份新礼物都会变得越来越具有互动性和复杂性。

sentences.en: Some were designed to be hung from a string and spun in the air.
sentences.zh: 有些被设计成用绳子悬挂并在空中旋转。

sentences.en: And as they rotate, some very interesting forms are created that are not visible when the form is stationary.
sentences.zh: 当它们旋转时，会产生一些非常有趣的形态，这些形态在静止时是看不见的。

sentences.en: Like a cube, for instance, looks like a cylinder when you spin it around fast enough.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你旋转得足够快时，立方体看起来就像一个圆柱体。

sentences.en: He wants the children to start to see that there are some invisible parts contained within the visible.
sentences.zh: 他希望孩子们开始看到，在可见物中包含着一些不可见的部分。

sentences.en: Next up came objects made up of smaller objects.
sentences.zh: 接下来是包含更小物体的物体。

sentences.en: Like a cube that breaks down into a bunch of little cubes.
sentences.zh: 比如一个可以拆解成一堆小立方体的立方体。

sentences.en: And then the toys would shift from being about perception to being about creation.
sentences.zh: 然后玩具会从关于“感知”转向关于“创造”。

sentences.en: They would become more versatile, pliant, and constructive.
sentences.zh: 它们会变得更加多功能、灵活和具有建设性。

sentences.en: Blocks gave way to paper, string, wire,
sentences.zh: 积木让位于纸张、绳子、金属丝，

sentences.en: little sticks and peas that could be connected and stacked into structures.
sentences.zh: 以及可以连接并堆叠成结构的小木棍和豌豆。

sentences.en: The objects would get more abstract and creative, leading to the final lesson.
sentences.zh: 物体会变得更加抽象和具有创造性，从而引出最后的课程。

sentences.en: The last is really just working freely with clay.
sentences.zh: 最后其实就是自由地使用粘土进行创作。

sentences.en: Clay being the most malleable of all.
sentences.zh: 粘土是所有材料中最具可塑性的。

sentences.en: It's rigid and it's soft.
sentences.zh: 它既坚硬又柔软。

sentences.en: And there's a whole range of things a child could build with it.
sentences.zh: 孩子可以用它建造各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: But even at this final stage,
sentences.zh: 但即使是在这最后阶段，

sentences.en: this wasn't the kind of creative free-for-all we tend to associate with childhood play.
sentences.zh: 这也不是我们通常与童年游戏联系在一起的那种创造性自由发挥。

sentences.en: Froebel had children sitting at desks, little workstations with grids laid out on them.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔让孩子们坐在课桌前，在带有网格的小工作台上操作。

sentences.en: So it's not free play.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是自由游戏。

sentences.en: The fact that the table has an underlying grid is very much at the root of the directed play.
sentences.zh: 桌子上有底层网格这一事实，正是这种引导式游戏的核心。

sentences.en: You follow instructions and there's an underlying order.
sentences.zh: 你遵循指令，并且存在一种潜在的秩序。

sentences.en: And so in this very structured, very Germanic way,
sentences.zh: 因此，以这种非常结构化、非常德国的方式，

sentences.en: the gifts encouraged students to think abstractly and to relate ideas, objects, and symbols.
sentences.zh: 这些礼物鼓励学生进行抽象思考，并将想法、物体和符号联系起来。

sentences.en: A set of blocks could be used to teach counting.
sentences.zh: 一套积木可以用来教数数。

sentences.en: Then the child could use those same blocks to build a house.
sentences.zh: 然后孩子可以用同样的积木盖房子。

sentences.en: And then tell stories of a family living in that house.
sentences.zh: 接着讲述住在那所房子里的一家人的故事。

sentences.en: So they were modeling the world in different ways, all using the same set of objects.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在用不同的方式模拟世界，而使用的都是同一套物体。

sentences.en: The children realized that they can create new shapes and new forms
sentences.zh: 孩子们意识到他们可以创造出新的形状和新的形式，

sentences.en: that they create on top of the gridded table.
sentences.zh: 这些形式是他们在网格桌上创造出来的。

sentences.en: These kindergartens weren't just schools.
sentences.zh: 这些幼儿园不仅仅是学校。

sentences.en: They were art schools, without all the sex and drugs and clove cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 它们是艺术学校，只是没有那些性、毒品和丁香烟。

sentences.en: They were places that taught about shape and form and color.
sentences.zh: 它们是教授形状、形式和色彩的地方。

sentences.en: And when kindergarten graduates went out into the world, the world changed.
sentences.zh: 当幼儿园毕业生走向世界时，世界改变了。

sentences.en: The kind of art that was being made in the 19th century is really different
sentences.zh: 19世纪创作的艺术类型，与孩子们上过幼儿园之后创作的艺术类型，

sentences.en: than the kind of art that was made after kids went to kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 确实非常不同。

sentences.en: Expressionist, cubist, and surrealist artists like Paul Klee and Vasily Kandinsky
sentences.zh: 像保罗·克利和瓦西里·康定斯基这样的表现主义、立体主义和超现实主义艺术家，

sentences.en: attended early kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 都上过早期的幼儿园。

sentences.en: Others, like Pete Mondrian, encountered Frobelian methods as teachers.
sentences.zh: 其他人，如皮特·蒙德里安，则作为教师接触过福禄贝尔的方法。

sentences.en: And when you look at a lot of their work,
sentences.zh: 当你观察他们的许多作品时，

sentences.en: alongside illustrations in kindergarten teacher guides,
sentences.zh: 再对比幼儿园教师指南中的插图，

sentences.en: the resemblance is uncanny.
sentences.zh: 这种相似性令人不可思议。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just artists.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是艺术家。

sentences.en: Kindergarten influenced designers, too.
sentences.zh: 幼儿园也影响了设计师。

sentences.en: Walter Gropius started the Bauhaus in 1919.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·格罗皮乌斯于1919年创办了包豪斯。

sentences.en: Gropius decided to hire a kindergarten teacher
sentences.zh: 格罗皮乌斯决定聘请一位幼儿园老师，

sentences.en: as the first hire of this famous school of design.
sentences.zh: 作为这所著名设计学院的第一位雇员。

sentences.en: So the Bauhaus had its adult design students doing geometric exercises,
sentences.zh: 因此，包豪斯的成年设计学生们也在做几何练习，

sentences.en: much like those found in kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 就像在幼儿园里发现的那样。

sentences.en: And the effects of Frobel's work on design education
sentences.zh: 而福禄贝尔的工作对设计教育的影响，

sentences.en: rippled out beyond Germany.
sentences.zh: 波及到了德国之外。

sentences.en: And some of his most explicit and direct influences can be found
sentences.zh: 他最明确、最直接的一些影响可以在

sentences.en: among the world's most famous architects.
sentences.zh: 世界上最著名的建筑师身上找到。

sentences.en: Frank Lloyd Wright, the American architect, is the great child of the kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 美国建筑师弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特是幼儿园的伟大结晶。

sentences.en: You can find a kindergarten in everything Wright ever did.
sentences.zh: 在赖特所做的一切中，你都能找到幼儿园的影子。

sentences.en: Frank Lloyd Wright was born in 1867,
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特出生于1867年，

sentences.en: around the time kindergartens were gaining traction in the United States.
sentences.zh: 那正是幼儿园在美国开始兴起的时候。

sentences.en: And his mom took classes in kindergarten education.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲曾修读过幼儿园教育课程。

sentences.en: Wright never went to architecture school,
sentences.zh: 赖特从未上过建筑学院，

sentences.en: but he recalls that when he was young,
sentences.zh: 但他回忆说，在他小时候，

sentences.en: his mother brought home a set of Frobel's gifts.
sentences.zh: 母亲带回家一套福禄贝尔教具。

sentences.en: Wright said that the moment he was given Frobel's gifts,
sentences.zh: 赖特说，就在他拿到福禄贝尔教具的那一刻，

sentences.en: he, quote, began to be an architect.
sentences.zh: 他，引用他的话，开始成为一名建筑师。

sentences.en: He went on to say,
sentences.zh: 他接着说，

sentences.en: For several years, I sat at that little kindergarten table,
sentences.zh: “好几年里，我坐在那张小小的幼儿园桌子旁，

sentences.en: ruled by lines about four inches apart.
sentences.zh: 桌面上画着间距约四英寸的线条。

sentences.en: But the smooth cardboard triangles and maplewood blocks were most important.
sentences.zh: 但那些光滑的纸板三角形和枫木积木才是最重要的。

sentences.en: All are in my fingers to this day.
sentences.zh: 至今，这些触感仍留在我的指尖。”

sentences.en: And Wright wasn't the only one.
sentences.zh: 而且赖特并非个例。

sentences.en: European modernist Le Corbusier also never went to architecture school.
sentences.zh: 欧洲现代主义者勒·柯布西耶也从未上过建筑学院。

sentences.en: But he did attend Frobelian schools in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在瑞士上过福禄贝尔式的学校。

sentences.en: The gridded geometries and repeated patterns of Le Corbusier's modernist houses and apartment blocks
sentences.zh: 勒·柯布西耶的现代主义住宅和公寓大楼中那些网格化的几何图形和重复的图案，

sentences.en: look like they were drawn on those gridded kindergarten desks.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像是在那些画着网格的幼儿园课桌上画出来的一样。

sentences.en: Le Corbusier and Frank Lloyd Wright,
sentences.zh: 勒·柯布西耶和弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特，

sentences.en: considered by some the two most important architects of the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 被一些人认为是20世纪最重要的两位建筑师，

sentences.en: had exactly the same childhood education.
sentences.zh: 他们接受的童年教育完全相同。

sentences.en: And then there's Buckminster Fuller,
sentences.zh: 还有巴克敏斯特·富勒，

sentences.en: famous for pioneering geodesic domes made up of triangles.
sentences.zh: 他以开创由三角形组成的测地线穹顶而闻名。

sentences.en: Fuller discovered his greatest engineering insight as a kindergartener,
sentences.zh: 富勒在幼儿园时期发现了自己最伟大的工程洞见，

sentences.en: connecting Frobelian peas and sticks.
sentences.zh: 当时他正在连接福禄贝尔的豌豆和木棍。

sentences.en: If you know Buckminster Fuller, this is the thing he's most famous for.
sentences.zh: 如果你了解巴克敏斯特·富勒，这正是他最出名的地方。

sentences.en: You know, the domes made out of peas and sticks, basically, nodes and rods.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些基本上由豌豆和木棍，也就是节点和杆件组成的穹顶。

sentences.en: So he learned that in kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在幼儿园学会这些的。

sentences.en: Obviously, not everyone who attended kindergarten
sentences.zh: 显然，并不是每个上过幼儿园的人

sentences.en: became a Frank Lloyd Wright or a Le Corbusier or a Bucky.
sentences.zh: 都成为了弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特、勒·柯布西耶或巴基那样的人。

sentences.en: But the abstract lessons of kindergarten tilled and fertilized the ground
sentences.zh: 但幼儿园的抽象课程耕耘并肥沃了土壤，

sentences.en: so the seeds of their ideas could find purchase in the world.
sentences.zh: 让他们的思想种子得以在世界上扎根。

sentences.en: Abstraction was accepted fairly quickly in Paris and in Europe.
sentences.zh: 抽象艺术在巴黎和欧洲被接受得相当快。

sentences.en: Perhaps because children had already been doing a lot of the same kinds of things for many decades,
sentences.zh: 也许是因为孩子们几十年来一直在做很多类似的事情，

sentences.en: that was one of the reasons that they were not so shocked when art turned in that direction.
sentences.zh: 这也是当艺术转向那个方向时，他们没有感到那么震惊的原因之一。

sentences.en: So in terms of 20th century art and design,
sentences.zh: 所以就20世纪的艺术和设计而言，

sentences.en: kindergarten was an absolute triumph.
sentences.zh: 幼儿园是一个绝对的胜利。

sentences.en: But Friedrich Frobel only got to witness the spread of his vision
sentences.zh: 但弗里德里希·福禄贝尔只目睹了他的愿景传播了

sentences.en: for about a decade before it was cut short.
sentences.zh: 大约十年，之后就被打断了。

sentences.en: In the 1850s, the Prussian government was cracking down on liberal thought.
sentences.zh: 19世纪50年代，普鲁士政府开始打击自由思想。

sentences.en: And in 1851, they issued the Kindergartenverbot,
sentences.zh: 1851年，他们发布了《幼儿园禁令》，

sentences.en: a national ban on kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内禁止幼儿园。

sentences.en: And Frobel died the very next year.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔在第二年就去世了。

sentences.en: And, you know, you wonder if he died of a broken heart in 1852.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，他是不是在1852年因心碎而死。

sentences.en: Of course, who knows?
sentences.zh: 当然，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But even though the ban slowed the expansion of kindergartens in Germany,
sentences.zh: 但尽管禁令减缓了幼儿园在德国的扩张，

sentences.en: it didn't stop the idea from spreading elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 它并没有阻止这一理念在其他地方传播。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: A lot of free-thinking liberals left Germany,
sentences.zh: 许多思想自由的进步人士离开了德国，

sentences.en: and they brought Frobel's kindergarten with them.
sentences.zh: 他们把福禄贝尔的幼儿园也带走了。

sentences.en: So his disciples, they were so dedicated to the work that they immigrated,
sentences.zh: 他的追随者们对这项工作非常投入，以至于他们选择了移民，

sentences.en: many of them to the United States.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人去了美国。

sentences.en: And basically, because of the ban,
sentences.zh: 基本上，正是因为这项禁令，

sentences.en: that's what led to Frobel's theories to be known around the world.
sentences.zh: 才导致福禄贝尔的理论闻名于世。

sentences.en: And the most dedicated kindergarten evangelists were women.
sentences.zh: 而最敬业的幼儿园传道者是女性。

sentences.en: As Tamar Zinger points out in her book, Architecture in Play,
sentences.zh: 正如塔玛·辛格在她的书《游戏中的建筑》中所指出的，

sentences.en: Frobel believed that women should play a leading role in educating children.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔认为女性应该在教育儿童方面发挥主导作用。

sentences.en: To be clear, Frobel wasn't exactly a feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，福禄贝尔算不上是个女权主义者。

sentences.en: He had very traditional ideas about gender roles
sentences.zh: 他对性别角色有着非常传统的看法，

sentences.en: and believed that it was the role of women to nurture children
sentences.zh: 并认为女性的角色就是作为保姆和幼儿园老师

sentences.en: as nannies and kindergarten teachers.
sentences.zh: 来养育孩子。

sentences.en: But regardless of Frobel's reasoning,
sentences.zh: 但无论福禄贝尔的理由是什么，

sentences.en: teaching kindergarten was a rare opportunity.
sentences.zh: 教幼儿园是一次难得的机会。

sentences.en: It was one of the only jobs you could get as a young woman.
sentences.zh: 这是年轻女性当时能找到的为数不多的工作之一。

sentences.en: There weren't many jobs.
sentences.zh: 当时的工作岗位并不多。

sentences.en: And it was women who drew up and translated the lesson books
sentences.zh: 正是女性编写并翻译了教学手册，

sentences.en: that would be used to teach a generation of young artists and designers.
sentences.zh: 这些手册后来被用来教育一代年轻的艺术家和设计师。

sentences.en: By 1885, there were over 500 kindergartens in America,
sentences.zh: 到1885年，美国已经有超过500所幼儿园，

sentences.en: and they were taught primarily by women.
sentences.zh: 而且它们主要由女性任教。

sentences.en: And you might be thinking,
sentences.zh: 你可能在想，

sentences.en: hey, I went to kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我也上过幼儿园。

sentences.en: Why didn't I grow up with this incredibly Germanic,
sentences.zh: 为什么我长大时没有接触到这种极其德国化的、

sentences.en: immaculately planned sequence of toys?
sentences.zh: 精心规划的玩具序列呢？

sentences.en: Well, ironically, the passion of some of kindergarten's biggest proponents
sentences.zh: 嗯，具有讽刺意味的是，幼儿园一些最大支持者的热情，

sentences.en: is part of the reason why you probably didn't grow up
sentences.zh: 正是你可能没有在成长过程中

sentences.en: playing with Frobel's gifts.
sentences.zh: 玩过福禄贝尔教具的部分原因。

sentences.en: The first kindergarten in the United States started in Watertown, Wisconsin in 1856,
sentences.zh: 美国的第一所幼儿园于1856年在威斯康星州的沃特敦开办，

sentences.en: but it was German language only.
sentences.zh: 但它只使用德语教学。

sentences.en: The educator Elizabeth Peabody was inspired by this kindergarten
sentences.zh: 教育家伊丽莎白·皮博迪受到这所幼儿园的启发，

sentences.en: and went on to found the first American English language kindergarten in Boston in 1860.
sentences.zh: 于1860年在波士顿创办了第一所美国英语幼儿园。

sentences.en: Peabody wanted to spread the teachings of Frobel to as many children as possible,
sentences.zh: 皮博迪希望将福禄贝尔的教导传播给尽可能多的孩子，

sentences.en: and so she reached out to Milton Bradley, the famous board game maker.
sentences.zh: 于是她联系了著名的棋盘游戏制造商米尔顿·布拉德利。

sentences.en: She wanted Bradley to mass-produce Frobel's gifts so that he could be accessible to everyone.
sentences.zh: 她希望布拉德利能大规模生产福禄贝尔教具，让每个人都能接触到。

sentences.en: And Milton Bradley, having heard her, was convinced,
sentences.zh: 米尔顿·布拉德利听了之后被说服了，

sentences.en: and since that moment, it turned his entire attention to the manufacture of Frobel blocks and gifts.
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，他将全部精力转向了福禄贝尔积木和教具的制造。

sentences.en: But where Peabody saw an educational ideal, Bradley saw a business opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但皮博迪看到的是教育理想，而布拉德利看到的是商业机会。

sentences.en: Bradley began adding a bunch of new toys into the mix,
sentences.zh: 布拉德利开始在产品中加入大量新玩具，

sentences.en: and then other manufacturers got in on the game too,
sentences.zh: 然后其他制造商也加入了这场游戏，

sentences.en: making all different kinds of stuff and just calling it all kindergarten toys.
sentences.zh: 制造各种各样的东西，并统称为幼儿园玩具。

sentences.en: He just made up stuff and he said,
sentences.zh: 他只是编造了一些东西，然后说，

sentences.en: this is kindergarten, and this is kindergarten, and this is kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 这是幼儿园玩具，这是幼儿园玩具，这也是幼儿园玩具。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily Frobel's kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是福禄贝尔的幼儿园教具。

sentences.en: The simple abstractions of Frobel's gifts had gone commercial.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔教具中简单的抽象概念已经商业化了。

sentences.en: And within a few years, Elizabeth Peabody went from promoting the manufacture of kindergarten toys
sentences.zh: 几年之内，伊丽莎白·皮博迪就从推广幼儿园玩具的生产，

sentences.en: to speaking out against it.
sentences.zh: 转变为公开反对它。

sentences.en: The interest of manufacturers and of merchants of the gifts and materials is a snare.
sentences.zh: “教具和材料的制造商与商人的利益是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: It has already corrupted the simplicity of Frobel in Europe and America,
sentences.zh: 它已经腐蚀了福禄贝尔在欧洲和美国所倡导的纯粹性，

sentences.en: for his idea was to use elementary forms exclusively and simple materials.
sentences.zh: 因为他的理念是专门使用基本形式和简单的材料。”

sentences.en: Even the word kindergarten itself became a generic term,
sentences.zh: 甚至“幼儿园”这个词本身也变成了一个通用术语，

sentences.en: a catch-all for early childhood education of all different kinds.
sentences.zh: 成了各种幼儿教育的统称。

sentences.en: These days, most kindergartens are a lot different from anything Frobel imagined,
sentences.zh: 如今，大多数幼儿园与福禄贝尔想象的完全不同，

sentences.en: and few kids encounter those early gifts in any kind of sequence, if at all.
sentences.zh: 很少有孩子能按任何顺序接触到那些早期的教具，甚至根本接触不到。

sentences.en: But kids still play with blocks.
sentences.zh: 但孩子们仍然在玩积木。

sentences.en: I mean, I really think that it's because of Frobel or Foible or however it's correctly pronounced,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真的认为正是因为福禄贝尔（无论名字怎么发音），

sentences.en: that children in the Western world play with blocks.
sentences.zh: 西方世界的孩子们才会玩积木。

sentences.en: But I think also blocks are constant across a variety of educational systems
sentences.zh: 但我认为积木在各种教育体系中都是恒久不变的，

sentences.en: because there's so much in them that they can teach.
sentences.zh: 因为它们能教授的东西实在太多了。

sentences.en: That's Alexandra Lang, an architecture critic and author of
sentences.zh: 那是亚历山德拉·朗，一位建筑评论家，也是

sentences.en: The Design of Childhood, How the Material World Shapes Independent Kids.
sentences.zh: 《童年的设计：物质世界如何塑造独立的孩子》一书的作者。

sentences.en: The block is this incredibly malleable toy that can be used in all of these different ways.
sentences.zh: 积木是一种极其灵活的玩具，可以用在所有这些不同的方式中。

sentences.en: Frobel wasn't the only one to see educational value in blocks.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔并不是唯一一个看到积木教育价值的人。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, Carolyn Pratt debuted her unit blocks.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，卡罗琳·普拉特推出了她的单元积木。

sentences.en: Unit blocks, which are essentially those classic brick-shaped pale wood blocks
sentences.zh: 单元积木，本质上就是那些经典的砖块状浅色木积木，

sentences.en: that really I can't think of any early childhood classroom I've been to that doesn't have those blocks.
sentences.zh: 我实在想不出我参观过的哪个幼儿教室里没有这些积木。

sentences.en: In some ways, all modern toy blocks were influenced by Frobel.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，所有现代玩具积木都受到了福禄贝尔的影响。

sentences.en: Tinker toys and Lego and Kinects, they're all about understanding shape and form and making connections.
sentences.zh: Tinker Toys、乐高和Kinects，它们都是关于理解形状、形式和建立联系。

sentences.en: But they also represent a departure from Frobel's highly organized and linear approach.
sentences.zh: 但它们也代表了对福禄贝尔高度组织化和线性方法的背离。

sentences.en: You know, the Frobel blocks, you were supposed to proceed from 1 to 20 through his exercises,
sentences.zh: 你知道，福禄贝尔积木，你应该通过他的练习从第1步进行到第20步，

sentences.en: whereas the unit blocks are much more open-ended.
sentences.zh: 而单元积木则开放得多。

sentences.en: They're more like we tend to encounter blocks today.
sentences.zh: 它们更像我们今天接触积木的方式。

sentences.en: These days, we don't think that blocks need an accompanying gridded desk or a syllabus of objects.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们不认为积木需要配套的网格桌或物体教学大纲。

sentences.en: Now blocks are creative tools for children that give them a chance to use their imagination
sentences.zh: 现在，积木是孩子们的创意工具，让他们有机会发挥想象力，

sentences.en: as they build houses and cities and interact with each other.
sentences.zh: 在建造房屋和城市以及相互交流时使用它们。

sentences.en: That's what I see when my boys play with Legos or build castles in Minecraft.
sentences.zh: 这就是我看到我的孩子们玩乐高或在《我的世界》里建造城堡时所看到的。

sentences.en: There isn't this sense of strict progression.
sentences.zh: 没有那种严格的进阶感。

sentences.en: It's more a sense that these blocks are a tool for children to recreate their own world as best they can.
sentences.zh: 更多的是一种感觉，即这些积木是孩子们尽其所能重建自己世界的工具。

sentences.en: And who knows how many architects, builders, designers, and thinkers
sentences.zh: 谁知道有多少建筑师、建造者、设计师和思想家，

sentences.en: all started with these literal building blocks, Frobelian or otherwise,
sentences.zh: 都是从这些实实在在的积木（无论是福禄贝尔式的还是其他的）开始，

sentences.en: learning creativity through construction.
sentences.zh: 通过构建来学习创造力的呢？

sentences.en: Frank Lloyd Wright's son, John, also went to kindergarten and also became an architect.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的儿子约翰也上过幼儿园，也成为了一名建筑师。

sentences.en: His most famous creation wasn't a building,
sentences.zh: 他最著名的作品不是建筑物，

sentences.en: but little kids have been building with it for over 100 years.
sentences.zh: 但小孩子们已经用它建造了100多年了。

sentences.en: That story after this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后继续讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: So I'm back with Kurt Kolstad to talk about another designer and Frank Lloyd Wright's family,
sentences.zh: 我又和库尔特·科尔斯塔德在一起，谈论另一位设计师和弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的家庭，

sentences.en: his son, John, who is also educated using Frobelian methods.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子约翰，他也接受了福禄贝尔方法的教育。

sentences.en: But what is really great about this story is that it culminates into one very particular design,
sentences.zh: 但这个故事真正精彩的地方在于，它最终指向了一个非常独特的设计，

sentences.en: that is his claim to fame.
sentences.zh: 那正是他成名的原因。

sentences.en: Yes, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it all started with Frank's mother, Anna, who is John's grandmother.
sentences.zh: 这一切都始于弗兰克的母亲安娜，也就是约翰的祖母。

sentences.en: Frank wrote and talked a lot about how Frobel's gifts led him to architecture.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克写过也谈论过很多关于福禄贝尔教具如何引导他走向建筑学的故事。

sentences.en: But it didn't hurt that his mom had wanted him to be an architect from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 但他的母亲从一开始就希望他成为一名建筑师，这对他很有帮助。

sentences.en: So she brought home Frobel's gifts as part of this grand agenda.
sentences.zh: 所以她把福禄贝尔教具带回家，作为这个宏大计划的一部分。

sentences.en: And sure enough, Frank went into architecture as planned.
sentences.zh: 果然，弗兰克按计划进入了建筑行业。

sentences.en: And eventually, he had kids of his own.
sentences.zh: 最终，他也有了自己的孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what I know about Frank Lloyd Wright's personal life is that
sentences.zh: 但我所了解的弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的个人生活是，

sentences.zh: 他与子女等人的家庭关系极其紧张且困难。

sentences.en: Yeah, there was a lot of heartache in that family,
sentences.zh: 没错，那个家庭里有很多心碎的往事，

sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是多个家庭，因为他结过好几次婚。

sentences.en: And the care of his children in the midst of all this often fell to the women in his life.
sentences.zh: 而在这一切之中，照顾孩子的重任往往落在了他生命中的女性身上。

sentences.en: And early in his career, while he's busy practicing architecture in Chicago,

sentences.zh: 他的母亲和第一任妻子凯瑟琳基本上就在隔壁教孩子们。

sentences.en: They effectively ran a kind of neighborhood kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上经营着一种社区幼儿园。

sentences.en: And in that, they used the same toys and methods that Anna had used with Frank.
sentences.zh: 在幼儿园里，他们使用了安娜曾经教导弗兰克时所用的同样的玩具和方法。

sentences.en: So in a way, they were shaping the next generation of Wright's,

sentences.zh: 甚至可能还怀着让他们也能成为建筑师的想法。

sentences.zh: 她创造了这位未来的建筑明星，现在她已经准备好工具，准备着手培养下一个了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And sure enough, John, Wright's second son, eventually did follow in his father's footsteps.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，赖特的第二个儿子约翰最终确实追随了他父亲的脚步。

sentences.en: Like, he went to school and dropped out, and he farmed for a while.
sentences.zh: 比如，他上过学，但中途退学了，还务农了一段时间。

sentences.zh: 而且他和他父亲并不总是合得来，所以他们渐行渐远。

sentences.en: But after John moved out to California, he started drafting.
sentences.zh: 但在约翰搬到加利福尼亚后，他开始从事绘图工作。

sentences.zh: 在那之后，他开始从事建筑实践。

sentences.en: And so after these years of estrangement, did they come together just like,
sentences.zh: 那么在经历了这些年的疏远之后，他们是因为都是建筑师，

sentences.zh: 所以才走到一起的吗？

sentences.zh: 这为他们提供了一个重新建立联系的契机，对吧？

sentences.zh: 他们最终确实一起工作了。

sentences.en: They traveled as a team to Japan for this really big and prestigious commission,
sentences.zh: 他们作为一个团队前往日本，承接了一个非常盛大且负有盛名的委托项目，

sentences.zh: 即东京的帝国饭店。

sentences.en: So while working on this project, both of the Wrights learned a lot about regional design strategies,

sentences.zh: 以及那些非常精妙且美观的木质互锁细木工技术。

sentences.en: So I've seen some of this joinery, but for people who can't quite picture it,
sentences.zh: 我见过一些这样的细木工，但对于那些无法想象的人来说，

sentences.en: could you describe it?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下吗？

sentences.en: I would love to be able to, but it's really hard.
sentences.zh: 我很想描述，但这真的很难。

sentences.en: But I can try.
sentences.zh: 但我可以试一试。

sentences.en: The basic idea is that instead of glue or nails,
sentences.zh: 基本理念是，无需胶水或钉子，

sentences.en: you could build structures made entirely out of these wooden pieces that slot and lock into one another.
sentences.zh: 你可以完全用这些相互嵌入和锁定的木块来建造结构。

sentences.en: The actual slot work, you really should just go online and look up,
sentences.zh: 至于实际的槽口工艺，你真的应该上网查一下，

sentences.en: because it's beautiful and it's intricate and very hard to describe.
sentences.zh: 因为它既美观又复杂，很难用语言描述。

sentences.en: But it all dates back to these ancient Chinese temples that were built this way.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都可以追溯到以这种方式建造的中国古代寺庙。

sentences.en: And later, Japan essentially adapted that technology to better withstand earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 后来，日本基本上采用了这项技术，以更好地抵御地震。

sentences.en: Between the flexibility of these joints and the flexibility of wood itself as a material,
sentences.zh: 得益于这些接头的灵活性以及木材本身作为材料的柔韧性，

sentences.en: a whole building can essentially sway instead of just shaking
sentences.zh: 整座建筑基本上可以摇摆，而不是仅仅震动，

sentences.en: and maybe even shaking itself apart during an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能在地震中把自己震散架。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: And that's particularly true if they're set up on a more flexible foundation.
sentences.zh: 如果它们安装在更灵活的地基上，情况尤其如此。

sentences.en: Okay, so Frank and John, they're in Japan, they're learning about joinery,
sentences.zh: 好的，所以弗兰克和约翰在日本，他们正在学习细木工，

sentences.zh: 在它建成后不久，东京发生了一场大地震，但酒店幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Still, despite the success of the project, it became a catalyst for another falling out between Frank and John,
sentences.zh: 尽管项目取得了成功，但它却成了弗兰克和约翰之间又一次决裂的导火索，

sentences.en: over salary this time.
sentences.zh: 这次是因为薪水问题。

sentences.en: But that experience of moving away from his father again led John to what became his claim to fame,
sentences.zh: 但那次再次远离父亲的经历，引导约翰走上了他成名之路，

sentences.en: which was architectural and built on all of his experiences to date,
sentences.zh: 那是一项建筑成就，建立在他迄今为止的所有经验之上，

sentences.en: but it wasn't actually a building at all.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上根本不是一座建筑。

sentences.zh: 1916年，约翰·劳埃德·赖特发明了林肯原木积木（Lincoln Logs）。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Lincoln Logs.
sentences.zh: 林肯原木积木。

sentences.zh: 我对林肯原木积木非常熟悉。

sentences.zh: 对于那些可能无法想象它们的人——如果你想象不出，我为你感到遗憾——

sentences.zh: 它们主要由这些长而圆的木棍组成。

sentences.en: They have notches in them.
sentences.zh: 它们上面有凹槽。

sentences.zh: 但这确实是一种制作微型小木屋的可爱而优雅的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 所以约翰想出了这个非常巧妙且简单的设计，

sentences.zh: 而且在第一次世界大战结束时，它们很快就投入了生产，

sentences.zh: 因为在战争期间，大量的金属被重新分配以支持盟军。

sentences.en: So wood was more readily available,
sentences.zh: 所以木材更容易获得，

sentences.zh: 而且很多金属玩具最终从货架上消失了，对吧？

sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.zh: 嗯，但它们最神奇的地方在于它们至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: Do you know how much they evolved from that original design that John did in 1916?
sentences.zh: 你知道它们与约翰在1916年做的那个原始设计相比进化了多少吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've actually looked up sets from different eras,
sentences.zh: 是的，我实际上查过不同时代的套装，

sentences.en: and remarkably, they haven't changed that much.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，它们并没有太大的变化。

sentences.en: My dad had a set when he was growing up that was a lot like mine,
sentences.zh: 我爸爸小时候有一套，和我小时候他给我买的那套很像，

sentences.en: that he got me when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我小时候他给我买的那套。

sentences.en: And today, my nieces, his grandchildren,
sentences.zh: 而今天，我的侄女们，也就是他的孙女们，

sentences.zh: 仍然喜欢玩他给我的那套玩具。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of like the Froebel's gift that we talked about,
sentences.zh: 是的，这有点像我们之前谈到的福禄贝尔教具（Froebel's gift），

sentences.en: you know, like they're passed on from generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像它们一代又一代地传下去一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, they're passed on like Froebel's gifts,
sentences.zh: 是的，它们像福禄贝尔教具一样传下去，

sentences.en: but they're not exactly like Froebel's gifts,
sentences.zh: 但它们并不完全等同于福禄贝尔教具，

sentences.en: at least according to Professor Marzinger,
sentences.zh: 至少根据马辛格教授的说法，

sentences.en: who we talked to earlier about these, right?
sentences.zh: 我们之前和她谈过这些，对吧？

sentences.zh: 你只能盖一个小木屋。

sentences.zh: 而且他发明的第一个版本，你只能盖一个木屋。

sentences.zh: 它们确实只能盖一个小木屋，你知道，

sentences.zh: 而且作为小木屋的微缩模型，它们很漂亮，

sentences.en: but that's where it ends.
sentences.zh: 但也就仅此而已了。

sentences.en: But a beautiful miniature log cabin is a pretty good end result.

sentences.zh: 还有比这更糟糕的结局。

sentences.zh: 关键是，它们就是玩具。

sentences.en: which are the Froebel's gifts.

sentences.zh: 但作为玩具，它们，你知道，直观、易学，

sentences.zh: 而且你可以盖一个小木屋。

sentences.zh: 但我甚至会争辩说，在某种程度上，它们比看起来更灵活，

sentences.zh: 如果你发挥想象力的话。

sentences.zh: 例如，我的侄女们会用玩具人偶来填充它们，

sentences.zh: 她们基本上赋予了它们生命，并用故事让它们活了起来。

sentences.zh: 所以我认为它们并不一定像最初看起来那样具有局限性。

sentences.zh: 但即使只是看玩具本身，

sentences.en: It's all pretty well designed.

sentences.zh: 或者不仅仅是小木屋的东西。

sentences.zh: 这些套装出现在20世纪初，

sentences.zh: 而那种建筑类型——小木屋，

sentences.zh: 真正触及了进步时代对边疆生活的一种怀旧情结。
